caption: The 60 fps budget is half of 30 fps and twice 120 fps; every CPU stage of a frame has to fit inside its 16.6 ms, and the rest is idle.
Render frames vary, but the accumulator always drains in whole 1/60 s steps: a 38 ms frame runs three ticks, a 12 ms frame may run none, and the remainder becomes alpha.
Frame B takes 17 ms and misses its vsync by 0.4 ms, so frame A stays on screen for 33.3 ms: a one-millisecond overrun costs a whole refresh.
A class tree shares behaviour along one axis, so the flying rideable barrel needs three parents; composition just attaches the components it needs to one entity.
Drawn at one pixel per byte: AoS drags in 7 cache lines to move 5 enemies, while SoA arrays move 42 enemies with 16 lines and use nearly every fetched byte.
The query walks only archetypes that have Position and Velocity, one contiguous array at a time; adding Health moves the entity into another table, a structural change.
Rotating the arm carries the hand and sword with it; their world matrices go dirty and are recomputed parents first.
The grid keeps 64 equal cells however the objects are spread; the quadtree splits only where the cluster is dense.
Frustum culling drops the four objects outside the view volume; occlusion culling then drops the two hidden behind the wall, leaving 3 of 9 to draw.
Same spring, same dt of 0.05 s: semi-implicit Euler tracks the exact curve, while explicit Euler gains energy every cycle until it leaves the chart.
The broad phase cuts 21 pairs to 3 by AABB overlap; the narrow phase rejects two false positives and returns one contact with a normal and depth.
At 2 m per step the bullet is before the 0.1 m fence at n and past it at n+1, so no overlap is ever seen; a swept test finds the hit at about 0.46 of the step.
